strengths: Comprehensive cross-modal evaluation demonstrating domain-agnostic applicability: consistent improvements on image, audio, human motion, and video generation with substantial speedups (8.75× on ImageNet 256×256)
Significant practical improvements with strong empirical results: 23.6% FID improvement on ImageNet, 20.7% FAD improvement on audio, and 7.7% FID improvement on human motion generation

Extensive ablation studies validating design choices: comprehensive analysis of layer selection (Tables 11-12), regularization coefficient sensitivity (Table 7), block dropping effects (Table 9), and gradient dynamics (Figure 7)
Well-motivated approach grounded in observations of representation quality hierarchy: the self-alignment principle is intuitive and empirically validated through representation analysis in Section G
Parameter-free, plug-and-play solution requiring no external models or additional data: easily adoptable by practitioners and composable with other methods (e.g., REPA)

Strong representation learning analysis: Section G provides compelling empirical evidence for the 'virtuous cycle' hypothesis, showing how internal alignment propagates improvements through the model hierarchy
Excellent reproducibility and clarity: detailed experimental procedures, rigorous methodology, and commitment to open-source all code and configurations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: the core technique (aligning normalized representations via cosine similarity) is straightforward and standard; the main contribution is identifying where to apply it rather than proposing novel methodology

Layer selection strategy lacks principled justification: the heuristic choices (exclude final 20%, exclude first layers, enforce 8-block distance) are empirically motivated without theoretical grounding; generalization to non-transformer architectures unclear
Incomplete computational overhead analysis: claims of 'negligible overhead' (abstract) lack quantification; no FLOPs breakdown or detailed timing analysis of LayerSync loss computation provided

Limited theoretical understanding of why the method works: while Section G provides empirical evidence, the paper lacks theoretical analysis of the optimization dynamics and convergence mechanisms underlying the improvement
Moderate hyperparameter sensitivity without clear guidance: λ robustness spans FID 36.19→31.36 (Table 7); no principled approach provided for selecting λ on new domains or tasks
Statistical significance under-reported: most results lack error bars; standard deviations in Table 6 (±0.8) are non-negligible relative to claimed improvements
Limited comparison with recent concurrent work: primary baseline is Dispersive Loss; insufficient comparison with other recent self-supervised regularization and representation learning methods
Underdeveloped video generation experiments: only 2 datasets tested despite claimed domain-agnosticity; video results relegated to appendix despite being integral to cross-modal claims
Unexplained discrepancy in audio results: 20.7% FAD improvement substantially exceeds image FID improvements (~10-12%), but paper does not discuss why or investigate this difference
Unclear architectural generalization: experiments on compact 8-layer models; scalability to very large models (100+ layers), CNNs, and other architectures not adequately addressed
